text: Which skeletal-muscle-specific genes stain strongly in myocytes and are never seen in the nucleoplasm?
plan: Tissue category (RNA): Skeletal muscle / Tissue enriched AND Tissue expression (IHC): Skeletal muscle / myocytes / High AND NOT Subcellular location (ICC): Nucleoplasm
understanding: The user is searching for genes showing tissue-specific expression in skeletal muscle, high immunohistochemical antibody staining in myocytes within skeletal muscle tissue, and an exclusion of localization to the nucleoplasm by immunocytochemistry.

trail.why: The question specifically asks for skeletal-muscle-specific genes, which corresponds to the category 'Tissue enriched' (at least four-fold higher mRNA level compared to any other tissue) in skeletal muscle.
Filtering for skeletal muscle myocytes with high IHC staining directly matches the requirement to identify genes that stain strongly in myocytes.
Selecting 'Nucleoplasm' at Level 1 with Level 2 unrestricted captures all genes observed in the nucleoplasm so they can be excluded.

requirements.why: This field defines RNA specificity across human tissues, including skeletal muscle specificity categories.
This field captures antibody staining levels per tissue (skeletal muscle) and specific cell type (myocytes).
This field annotates subcellular compartments detected by immunofluorescence, and negating it with NOT excludes genes localized to the nucleoplasm.
